newsitem.title: GERMANY: Brazils ease nearby tightness in German coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazils ease nearby tightness in German coffee.

text.p: Brazil arabicas helped ease short nearby supplies of Central American green coffees in Germany, traders said on Monday.
"Otherwise consumption is steady and supplies are adequeate," one said.
"Roasters can make do with Brazils but of course they are eagerly awaiting news of Central American and Colombian shipments and they would like better offers from Africa."
Arabica prices were generally too high and qualities barely sufficient to replace the Central American share in traditional blends, he added.
Traders said the tight situation should support the New York futures upside, with December ending at 117.25 cents/lb last Friday, at a 10.8 cents premium over March.
"The market wants to break higher but origin fixings above 120 cents are preventing this," another trader said.
He also pointed out the New York market was mostly reflecting U.S. tightness, where consumption had developed more strongly than in Europe and where stocks were at historic lows.
Brazils were readily available here as Brazilian exporters tried to cash in on the December premium before other origins become available.
In the Bremen import market, arabicas were mostly higher last week but Brazils were on offer at $110 per 50 kg fob versus $112 a week earlier.
Kenyans were up $1 at $158 and Indonesian robustas were off $2 at $61 cif.
